actions.diff:
--- a/minbpe/regex.py
+++ b/minbpe/regex.py
@@ -324,9 +324,48 @@
-        cache_get = cache.get
-        for chunk in text_chunks:
-            chunk_ids = cache_get(chunk)
-            if chunk_ids is None:
-                chunk_bytes = chunk.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
-                chunk_ids = self._encode_chunk(chunk_bytes, merge_lookup)
-                cache[chunk] = chunk_ids
-            ids.extend(chunk_ids)
-        return ids
+        order = self._get_merge_order()
+        if order is not None:
+            # encode all distinct uncached chunks together: one char per token,
+            # chunks joined by a separator that no merge contains, and each
+            # merge applied once in index order (see BasicTokenizer.encode)
+            missing = dict.fromkeys([c for c in text_chunks if c not in cache])
+            if missing:
+                sep, pairs = order
+                s = sep.join([c.encode("utf-8").decode("latin-1") for c in missing])
+                for pair, new in pairs:
+                    s = s.replace(pair, new)
+                for chunk, part in zip(missing, s.split(sep)):
+                    cache[chunk] = list(map(ord, part))
+            extend = ids.extend
+            for chunk in text_chunks:
+                extend(cache[chunk])
+            return ids
+        cache_get = cache.get
+        for chunk in text_chunks:
+            chunk_ids = cache_get(chunk)
+            if chunk_ids is None:
+                chunk_bytes = chunk.encode("utf-8") # raw bytes
+                chunk_ids = self._encode_chunk(chunk_bytes, merge_lookup)
+                cache[chunk] = chunk_ids
+            ids.extend(chunk_ids)
+        return ids
+
+    def _get_merge_order(self):
+        # (separator, [(pair str, merged str), ...] in merge index order) when
+        # every merge produces a distinct id larger than both of its inputs, so
+        # that applying the merges once in order matches _encode_chunk; else None
+        lookup = self._get_merge_lookup()
+        if getattr(self, "_merge_order_src", None) is not lookup:
+            order = None
+            if type(self)._encode_chunk is RegexTokenizer._encode_chunk:
+                ordered = sorted(self.merges.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
+                top = max([idx for _, idx in ordered], default=255)
+                if all(type(p0) is int and type(p1) is int and type(idx) is int
+                       and 0 <= p0 < idx and 0 <= p1 < idx
+                       for (p0, p1), idx in ordered) and \
+                        top + 1 < 0x110000 and \
+                        len({idx for _, idx in ordered}) == len(ordered):
+                    sep = chr(max(top, 255) + 1)
+                    order = (sep, [(chr(p0) + chr(p1), chr(idx))
+                                   for (p0, p1), idx in ordered])
+            self._merge_order = order
+            self._merge_order_src = lookup
+        return self._merge_order

actions.reason: No change reached the 1% bar for encode_ir. I tried one change in RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary. It joined the distinct uncached chunks with a separator character that no merge can contain, then applied each merge once, in index order, as a str.replace, and split the result back into chunks. Outputs matched the parent exactly, but encode_ir rose to 1.0128 of the parent and train_ir to 1.0084. I reverted the change, so the tree is back to the parent. The repository already caches encoded chunks, so the Python merge loop on cache misses seems to be a small part of the total. The 512 str.replace passes cost more than that loop. My guess, not measured, is that most of encode_ir is fixed cost: interpreter start, importing the regex package, compiling the split pattern, and probably compiling the minbpe sources on each run. The last point is suggested by train_ir rising when lines were added to code that training never runs. Moving the training code into a lazily imported module would cut that compile cost, but it would exceed the 200-line diff limit. Lazily importing unicodedata would save nothing, because the regex package already imports it.

journal.text:
I changed RegexTokenizer.encode_ordinary in minbpe/regex.py. The new version joined the distinct uncached chunks with a separator character that no merge can contain. It then applied each merge once, in index order, as a str.replace, and split the result back into chunks. I later reverted both edited regions.

One sandbox evaluation. Equivalence held and outputs were identical to the parent. encode_ir went from 409426275 to 414665831, ratio 1.0128, against a required 0.9900. train_ir went from 325891809 to 328635582, ratio 1.0084. The change did not help. It was rejected for no improvement, and I submitted no candidate.

The per-chunk cache already removes most repeated work. One pass of str.replace per merge across the joined text costs more than it saves, and the extra join and split add to that. encode_ir does not reward a change to batching shape alone.

Next, profile _encode_chunk on uncached chunks before editing anything. Measure how often the merge loop scans the pairs dict, and target that inner loop.
